column2: I have designed in the last two years several different campaigns on the German/Axis side or the Soviet side. Most of the scenarios were East-Front fighting. Histo rically most of the heaviest action occurred in the East Front within the period covered by the campaign (late 1942 - late 1945). Most of the casualties in WWII occurred in the Russian front (3/5 of all others combined). Therefore, the scenarios were fu l l of fast pace and violent action. The fighting was also extremely violent and continuous. Recently Mr. Frank Chini presented a campaign that was a combination of Onward to Berlin and Defending the Reich with the player being the German side. He develo p ed a procedure to reverse the players' sides, i.e., if originally the player was the German and the AI was the Soviets, he reversed the order. This campaign gave me the idea of collecting my more than 40 East-Front Scenarios together with the SSI scenari os and preparing a Russian campaign by retooling all these scenarios.

column2: This campaign has been designed to reflect fast pace, heavy and continuous action. In many s cenarios the player will be allowed to deploy only a fraction of its army. The auxiliary units are very important because they contribute to the balance of power and at the same time provide some sorely needed capabilities. At the same time the game bec o mes more realistic. Successful campaign play requires minimum casualties or you will be out pretty soon. This fact leads to neglect of the auxiliary units and excessive caution concerning the core units. Here you cannot neglect your auxiliary units. Y ou will need every single one of them or you will not win. I regularly reinforced them to keep them alive.

column2: One interesting concept used in this campaign is the idea of "defensive scenarios." There are several of these scenarios in the campaign. The mai n idea is, the player does not have neither victory nor supply objectives. In order to win the player has to keep all the victory objectives held by him at the beginning of the game. If some are lost the player has to retake them to win. Of course, the game is over if the player loses all of them. Mr. Lasse Jensen originally proposed this idea. It was implemented using his excellent editor. You set victory conditions for both players on the same hexes and then you make sure that at least one of your v ictory hexes is lost. I found out that 3-4 victory scenarios are the best number. One or two are practically lost from the beginning, and the other one-two is/are under very heavy attack. If you set the AI to attack mode and give adequate reinforcement s you have a nice game. The lack of supply hexes is used to reduce the number of player units.

column2: This campaign is not a historical campaign. I have a lot of respect for people who try to reproduce history, but this is mostly a fictional campaign. Everybody knows how things ended and it was a good thing. I designed a movement, heavy and continuous action campaign. You start fighting from the first term and it will not be over until is over. I sincerely regret if you do not like this kind of scenarios, but everybody is entitled to his own taste.
